transcript:
Header: 2026-11-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: James (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Dr Ellen Park (CISO), Marcus Lee (Head IT), Sara Velez (Legal), Kenji Ito (Cloud Arch)

Summary (auto): quick run through of CAIQ items, confirm KMS/BYOK approach and evidence delivery plan. Some cross talk on network peering and private deployment options.

[00:00] James Ortega: ok welcome everyone, thanks for making time this afternoon, this is James from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. how are you folks?
[00:12] Dr. Ellen Park: good thanks james. we wanted to focus on evidence for our vendor risk team — SOC 2, ISO, and specifically the KMS questions and data residency.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: yes and also audit logs retention, like how long are logs kept and are they exportable into our SIEM.
[00:27] James Ortega: absolutely, that's the plan. we'll walk through what we can provide today and then call out where we need to produce artifacts for your SIG or CAIQ. also flag any blockers like HSM/BYOK.
[00:36] Priya Nair: quick intro from my side — i'll cover KMS/HSM, key rotation, BYOK options, and how our private deployment works re: VPC peering.
[00:44] Kenji Ito: ok thanks, our agenda is basically: 1) compliance artifacts 2) KMS + BYOK architecture 3) network / residency. 4) timeline.

[02:05] Dr. Ellen Park: can you confirm you have SOC 2 Type II? our procurement requires it and ideally ISO 27001 as well.
[02:12] James Ortega: yes we have SOC 2 Type II for the platform, we'll send a redacted copy. we also hold ISO 27001 through last audit — we'll attach cert. these are in the security package i'll share after the call.
[02:30] Sara Velez: will the SOC2 report include user-level access logs or just control narrative? our legal/policy team needs the parts about privileged access and encryption.
[02:38] Priya Nair: the report is control-focused; for logs we provide audit log extracts and we can include an explanation of our RBAC model and how we log admin actions. we also have change-control evidence and pentest summaries.

[05:00] Marcus Lee: specifically on KMS — do you offer BYOK where our keys live in our KMS/HSM and you access them? or do you manage keys for customers?
[05:08] Priya Nair: we support multiple modes: Redwood-managed keys for hosted API, and BYOK for Dedicated/Private. BYOK can be via cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS, GCP KMS) or HSM-backed keys in a customer-managed HSM. there are a few tradeoffs — latency for remote key calls vs local keys in secure enclaves.
[05:28] Dr. Ellen Park: what about FIPS and HSM attestation? our auditors want evidence of HSM module levels and FIPS 140-2/3 compliance.
[05:35] Priya Nair: we can provide HSM vendor attestation and details on FIPS level where applicable. if you need a dedicated HSM we can talk through a private deployment with customer-managed HSM or a hosted HSM proxy. we'll prep a matrix.

[08:10] James Ortega: side note — for EU data residency we can pin workloads to EU regions and restrict egress. Kenji, does your architecture require full on-prem or just colocation in EU cloud regions?
[08:22] Kenji Ito: prefer cloud regions in EU initially, may look at on-prem later for certain PHI workflows. also need keys to stay in EU for EU-resident data.
[08:31] Priya Nair: that is doable — we support region pinning and can do BYOK with keys resident in EU KMS. there's complexity around cache and KV cache replication; we can configure TTLs and ensure cached KV doesn't cross boundaries.
[08:45] Marcus Lee: can you clarify "KV cache"? some of our reviewers think caching could leak data residency.
[08:51] Priya Nair: sure, our KV cache is per-region and we can enforce no cross-region replication for pinned models. note transcription: sometimes this gets written as K-V cash which is a bit messy in auto transcriptions.

[11:00] Dr. Ellen Park: audit logs — retention length? we need at least 2 years plus possibility to export to our SIEM.
[11:07] Priya Nair: default retention is 90 days in hosted; for Dedicated/Private we can extend retention or stream logs to your cloud storage/ SIEM. we generate structured audit events for token usage, admin actions, key operations.
[11:20] Marcus Lee: streaming — do you support syslog or Kafka?
[11:25] Priya Nair: we support HTTPS delivery, S3 sink, and Kafka integration for dedicated setups. we can also set up forwarders for syslog via a small connector.

[14:10] Sara Velez: on RBAC and SSO — we need SAML + SCIM for provisioning, role separation, admin vs developer roles. can you map that to our IdP?
[14:20] James Ortega: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. roles are standard: viewer, developer, admin, infra-admin; we can also add custom roles for enterprise. we keep an audit trail for role changes.
[14:34] Dr. Ellen Park: is there support for session recording or capturing impersonation events?
[14:40] Priya Nair: we log impersonation and privileged— there's an audit marker for session elevation events. full session recording is not part of the platform by default.

[18:30] Marcus Lee: procurement will ask about certificate rotation and key rotation policies. what's your default rotation cadence?
[18:36] Priya Nair: default key rotation is 90 days for service keys; customer BYOK rotation schedule can be customer-controlled. we document rotation policies and can provide rotation logs as evidence.

[21:00] Kenji Ito: network architecture for private deployments — can you do VPC peering or do you require a VPN?
[21:07] Priya Nair: we support VPC peering, PrivateLink-style connectors, and site-to-site VPN. for strict networks we'd recommend dedicated deployment with peering and private control plane.
[21:20] James Ortega: i want to call out a common objection: latency vs cryptographic safety. BYOK with remote key calls can add latency; for high throughput we recommend key caching in secure hardware with short-lived local keys derived from BYOK. we'll detail the tradeoffs in the diagram.

[25:00] Dr. Ellen Park: SIG / CAIQ — can you walk us through how you'll fill the CAIQ and what evidence you'll attach?
[25:08] James Ortega: yes, we typically return the CAIQ with direct evidence links. for items requiring attestation we'll provide SOC2 control IDs mapped, e.g., CC6, CC7... note transcription sometimes mangles those to C-C six, etc. we'll also include sample screenshots of console controls where relevant and redacted logs.
[25:35] Priya Nair: practical approach: you upload the CAIQ, mark the top 25 critical Qs you need answered first, and we'll prioritize. for evidence delivery we can either give you a shareable evidence bundle (S3 link with signed URLs) or push items into your secure intake (SFTP).

[29:10] Marcus Lee: are there any controls you typically can't provide evidence for?
[29:16] Priya Nair: we can't provide customer-specific data extracts beyond what the customer owns; also we won't provide lowered-level OS logs from multi-tenant infrastructure without a dedicated deployment due to shared host constraints. for those we'd recommend Dedicated or Private.

[32:50] Dr. Ellen Park: how long will the evidence assembly take? procurement is asking for a timeline.
[32:56] James Ortega: typical turnaround for a prioritized CAIQ subset is 3–7 business days for hosted artifacts; for Dedicated/private HSM attestations, plan for 10–15 business days depending on vendor attestation timing.

[36:00] Kenji Ito: encryption in transit — do you use mTLS between services and for public APIs?
[36:06] Priya Nair: yes TLS 1.2+ for public APIs and mTLS for internal service-to-service in Dedicated deployments; we can provide cipher suites and cert management docs.

[40:10] Sara Velez: legal needs to confirm data residency clause — we may ask for contract language that restricts processing to EU regions for certain data classes. can you accept that?
[40:20] James Ortega: yes contract language is standard for enterprise — we can include residency and processing location clauses for the POC and final contract. we'll share sample contract snippets.

[43:00] Marcus Lee: about log immutability — can you provide proof of write-once logs or tamper-evident audit trails?
[43:08] Priya Nair: we support append-only object stores for audit logs and can provide SHA256 checksums and signed manifests for an immutable trail. for higher assurance we can export to your WORM-configured object storage.

[46:30] Dr. Ellen Park: pen test evidence — do you have a recent external penetration test and findings?
[46:36] James Ortega: yes we have a pen test summary and remediation plan; we can provide redacted report and evidence of fixes.

[49:00] James Ortega: ok, quick recap before we wrap: we'll send security package + SOC2/ISO docs, Priya will make KMS/HSM diagram and BYOK workflow, customer to upload CAIQ and mark priority questions, and we'll schedule the HSM deep-dive. any objections to that plan?
[49:18] Dr. Ellen Park: sounds good. one question — for the POC can we restrict to EU-only data flow?
[49:24] Priya Nair: yes we can configure the POC for EU region pinning and BYOK in EU KMS to keep keys inside EU.

[51:00] Sara Velez: i'll follow up with legal questions and share contract clauses.
[51:05] Marcus Lee: i'll coordinate infra and get the CAIQ into you by monday.

[55:30] James Ortega: perfect. i'll put the notes and action items in the follow-up email and share a calendar invite for the HSM deep-dive. thanks everyone.
[55:40] Dr. Ellen Park: thank you.
[55:45] Priya Nair: thanks all.
[57:00] Call ended.
